newsitem.title: USA: OPTIONS - US T-bond vols edge up on supply, Fed.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS - US T-bond vols edge up on supply, Fed.

text.p: Implied volatilities for U.S. Treasury bond options edged up as bond prices slid on a weaker dollar, a huge corporate debt issue and remarks by Federal Reserve governor Laurence Meyer, dealers said.
The volatility gains were mostly confined to the shorter-dated options, which have higher gamma values and are sensitive to quick bond price movements, they noted, however.
"There's not much option traffic of any kind of size, yet we have seen volatilities pick up a little today," said a brokerage trader at the Chicago Board of Trade.
Implied volatility for March T-bond futures options stood at around 9.5 percent in early afternoon trading, up about 0.2 point from late Wednesday levels.

After a brief early rally, the bond market came under pressure from a six-tranche debt offering totaling $4.1 billion -- said to be the largest investment-grade corporate debt offering ever -- from US West Capital Funding, a unit of U S West Communications Group.
In one of the few large options deals in the CBOT pit, Merrill Lynch, lead manager of the U.S. West issue, was said to have sold 5,000 lots of February 110 puts.
"It probably has something to do with it (the US West offering)," the CBOT trader said. "They'd need to be a seller in futures, so that's probably a protection of some sort."
Later, comments by Fed's Meyer hit the market, buoying volatilities.

Meyer said he was slightly more concerned about faster inflation than slower growth and the Fed must act quickly on inflation if needed. He also said "a more forward-looking approach" to interest rate policy might become appropriate if the unemployment rate declined.
"The market definitely saw a little flurry there" after Meyer's comments, a Eurodollar trader for a bank affiliate at the Chicago Mercantile Exchange said.
"We'll see if there's any followthrough to that," he said, adding that he was still skeptical whether the Fed would raise interest rates at its Federal Open Market Committee meeting on February 4-5.
Implied volatility for CME June Eurodollar futures options was up about a quarter point at around 12.9 percent. September was steady at 15.2 percent, perhaps due to the contract's lower gamma.
